entries.title: Unparseable-by-sonic input returns verdict status 3, and the JS wrapper throws an internal-invariant error instead of falling back to the TS path
entries.rootCause: crates/zodrs/src/validate.rs returns Verdict{status:3} both for 'plan not JSON-eligible' (a compile-time fact) and for 'sonic_rs::from_slice rejected the input' (a runtime fact). packages/zodrs/src/core/parse.ts parseJson() case 3 treats every status 3 as the unreachable compile-time invariant and throws 'Internal invariant: native backend received a non-JSON-eligible plan'. The correct behavior for an eligible plan whose bytes sonic cannot parse is to fall back to the TS path (JSON.parse + TS validator), which per the plan 'reproduces any JSON.parse SyntaxError exactly'. Affected input classes: BOM prefix (TextDecoder strips it, JSON.parse succeeds, sonic rejects), lone-surrogate escapes like \ud800 (JSON.parse accepts, sonic rejects), 1e400 overflow (JSON.parse yields Infinity, sonic rejects), NaN/Infinity literals and truncated/malformed JSON (JSON.parse throws SyntaxError; safeParseJson must throw SyntaxError, not an invariant Error).

repro.refOutcome: safeParse(JSON.parse(...)) -> { success: true, data: { name: "Ada", age: 36 } }
repro.nativeOutcome: safeParseJson(bytes) throws Error: Internal invariant: native backend received a non-JSON-eligible plan

entries.title: Duplicate JSON object keys: Rust byte path keeps the FIRST occurrence, JSON.parse keeps the LAST
entries.rootCause: sonic-rs's borrowed DOM resolves duplicate object keys first-wins, while JSON.parse (ECMA-262) resolves them last-wins. For an input like {"name":"A","name":"Ada","age":36} against { name: z.string().min(3) }, the TS reference succeeds with "Ada" while the Rust path validates "A" and fails too_small. Fix direction: sonic-rs's Value object access must prefer the last occurrence (or the plan must treat any input with duplicate keys as status-3 fallback, since last-wins is observable behavior).

repro.refOutcome: safeParse(JSON.parse(...)) -> { success: true, data: { name: "Ada", age: 36 } } (last key wins)
repro.nativeOutcome: safeParseJson(bytes) -> { success: false, issues: [too_small @ path ["name"]] } (first key wins)

entries.title: Native byte path attaches non-canonical fields to issues: `input` on every issue and `origin` on invalid_format and not_multiple_of
entries.rootCause: Canonical zod v4 strips `input` from issue objects unless reportInput is true (.references/zod/packages/zod/src/v4/core/util.ts finalizeIssue: destructures input out, re-adds only when ctx.reportInput; ParseContext.reportInput defaults to false in schemas.ts). Vendored corpus snapshots confirm default safeParse issues carry no `input`. But packages/zodrs/src/core/parse.ts parseJson() status-2 branch calls makeError(raw, { ...context, reportInput: true }) after back-filling input on every raw issue, so safeParseJson failures always carry `input` where safeParse failures do not. Separately, the Rust issue serializer emits origin on invalid_format and not_multiple_of issues; the canonical shapes ($ZodIssueInvalidStringFormat errors.ts:70-75, $ZodIssueNotMultipleOf) have no origin field. Note: the plan's own §Verification-3(b) expectation showing input on byte-path issues contradicts canonical zod v4 behavior; the drop-in contract (and the differential invariant) outranks the plan text. Sub-note: native also leaves an own `input: undefined` property on invalid_union sub-issues (canonically absent) and does not backfill sub-issue inputs at all — see the separate union-sub-issue class in the fuzz report.

repro.refOutcome: safeParse(JSON.parse(...)) -> issues: [{ expected: "number", code: "invalid_type", path: [], message: "Invalid input: expected number, received array" }]
repro.nativeOutcome: safeParseJson(bytes) -> issues: [{ code: "invalid_type", expected: "number", path: [], message: "...", input: [[[1]]] }] (extra `input`)
